In mathematical analysis, '''Ehrenpreis's fundamental principle''', introduced by [[Leon Ehrenpreis]], states:<ref>{{cite book |doi=10.1007/978-1-4614-4075-8_24 |volume=28 | pages=491–507|series=Developments in Mathematics |year=2013 |last1=Treves |first1=François |title=From Fourier Analysis and Number Theory to Radon Transforms and Geometry |isbn=978-1-4614-4074-1 |chapter=Ehrenpreis and the Fundamental Principle }}</ref>
:Every solution of a system (in general, overdetermined) of homogeneous [[partial differential equation]]s with constant [[coefficient]]s can be represented as the integral with respect to an appropriate Radon measure over the complex “[[characteristic variety]]” of the system.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Oshima|first=Toshio|title=A Proof of Ehrenpreis' Fundamental Principle in Hyperfunctions|journal=Proceedings of the Japan Academy|volume=50|pages=16–18|url=http://projecteuclid.org/DPubS?service=UI&version=1.0&verb=Display&handle=euclid.pja/1195519103|accessdate=25 July 2013|doi=10.3792/pja/1195519103|year=1974|doi-access=free}}</ref>
